source_text: Ἀπὸ δὲ τούτων ἁπασῶν ἐμαυτὸν ἐπιστρέψας τῶν ἐννοιῶν κατεσκεψάμην καὶ ἀπεστράφην πάντα εἴδη συκοφαντιῶν τὰ ἐν ἀνθρώποις πλαζόμενα, ἐξ ὧν τινὲς μὲν ἀδικούμενοι δακρύουσι καὶ θρηνοῦσι, βίᾳ καταβεβλημένοι τῶν ἐπαμυνόντων, ἢ ὅλως παραμυθησομένων αὐτοὺς πάσης πανταχόθεν κατεχούσης ἀπορίας· οἱ δὲ χειροδίκαι εἰς ὕψος αἴρονται, ἐξ οὗ καὶ πεσοῦνται. Τῶν δὲ ἀδίκων καὶ θρασέων, οἱ μὲν ἀποθανόντες, ἄμεινον παρὰ τοὺς μέχρι νῦν ζῶντας ἔπραξαν. Αἱρετώτερος δὲ τούτων ἀμφοτέρων, ὁ ὅμοιος αὐτοῖς ἐσόμενος, μηδέπω δὲ γεγονώς, ὅτι οὔπω τῆς κατὰ ἀνθρώπους ἥψατο πονηρίας. Φανερὸν δέ μοι ἐγένετο καὶ ὁπόσος ἀνδρὶ φθόνος παρὰ τῶν πέλας ἕπεται, οἶστρος ὑπάρχων πονηροῦ πνεύματος· καὶ ὅτι ὁ ὑποδεξάμενός τε αὐτόν, καὶ οἱονεὶ προστερνισάμενος, οὐδὲν ἕτερον ἔχει, ἢ τὸ διεσθίειν τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ψυχήν, καὶ διαπρίειν τε καὶ δαπανᾶν μετὰ τοῦ σώματος ἑαυτοῦ λύπην ἀπαραμύθητον, τὴν τῶν ἄλλων εὐπραγίαν τιθέμενον. Ἕλοιτο δ᾽ ἄν τις εὖ φρονῶν θατέραν ἐμπλῆσαι τῶν χειρῶν, σὺν ῥᾳστώνῃ καὶ πραότητι, ἤπερ ἀμφοτέρας σὺν μόχθῳ, καὶ δολεροῦ πνεύματος πανουργίᾳ. Ἔστι δέ τι καὶ ἕτερον, ὅπερ οἶδα συμβαῖνον παρὰ τὸ προσῆκον, ἀνδρὸς ἕνεκα προαιρέσεως οὐκ ἀγαθῆς. Ὃς μεμονωμένος πάντοθεν, καὶ οὔτε ἀδελφὸν ἔχων, οὔτε υἱόν, κτήμασι δὲ πολλοῖς εὐθηνούμενος, ἀπληστίᾳ συζῶν, χρηστότητι ἑαυτὸν οὐθ᾽ ὅλως ὁτιοῦν ἐπιδοῦναι θέλει. Ἡδέως οὖν ἂν αὐτὸν ἐροίμην, ὅτου χάριν ὁ τοιοῦτος μοχθεῖ, τὸ μὲν ἀγαθόν τι δρᾶσαι προτροπάδην φεύγων, ποικίλαις δὲ τοῦ χρηματίσασθαί ποθεν ἐπιθυμίαις διασπώμενος.
thought_title: On oppression, envy, and the solitary miser
orientation: Solomon reflects on human oppression, the folly of envy, and the misery of a man who has no kin yet hoards wealth, refusing himself any enjoyment.
pass_a_gloss: From all these things, turning myself back from the thoughts, I examined and turned away from every kind of false accusation that wanders among humans; from which some, being wronged, weep and lament, having been thrown down by force by those who defend them, or altogether being comforted by nothing, since helplessness holds them on every side; but the wrongdoers are lifted up to a height, from which also they will fall. Of the unjust and bold, those who have died have fared better than those living until now. More preferable than both of these is the one who will be like them, but has not yet come to be, because he has not yet touched the wickedness that belongs to humans. It became clear to me also how much envy follows a man from those near him, being a goad of an evil spirit; and that the one who received it, and who as it were struck his breast beforehand, has nothing else except to eat away his own soul, and to saw through and to spend with his own body an inconsolable grief, setting the prosperity of others before him. A sensible person would choose to fill one of the hands with ease and meekness, rather than both hands with toil and the cunning of a deceitful spirit. There is also another thing, which I know happens contrary to what is fitting, for the sake of a man's choice not good. He who is isolated on every side, and has neither brother nor son, yet thriving with many possessions, living with insatiability, is not willing to grant himself any kindness at all. I would gladly ask him, for the sake of what such a man toils, eagerly fleeing doing any good thing, being torn apart by varied desires to acquire wealth from somewhere.

lemmas.gloss: wrongdoers (lit. doing wrong with the hand)

choices.why: Classical sense of slanderous charge or blackmail; the context describes oppression that wanders among humans.
Literal 'those who do wrong with the hand'; matches the contrast with the wronged who weep.
Refers to receiving envy; 'it' is the envy just mentioned.
Vivid physical gesture of grief/anticipation; keeps the compound verb's force.

choices.english: the cunning of a deceitful spirit
choices.why: Panourgia is cunning/craft; dolerou modifies spirit. Contrasted with ease and meekness.
rejected: the cleverness of a guileful spirit
the knavery of a tricky spirit

choices.why: Standard gloss for the vice of never having enough; the man thrives in possessions but lives in this condition.

pass_b_english: Turning myself away from all these reflections, I looked closely; I turned away from every kind of false accusation that wanders among people. Some are wronged — they weep and lament, thrown down by force, with no one to defend them or comfort them at all, helplessness pressing on every side. Wrongdoers are lifted up to a height from which they will also fall. Of the wicked and the insolent, those who have died are better off than those still living. Better than both is the one who will be like them but has not yet come into being, because he has not yet touched the wickedness that belongs to human life. It also became clear to me how much envy follows a person from his neighbors — a goad of an evil spirit. The one who receives it, who takes it in and, as it were, clasps it to his breast, has nothing else but the consuming of his own soul, sawing and spending his own inconsolable grief along with his body, making the prosperity of others the cause of his grief. A sensible person would rather fill one hand with ease and meekness than both hands with toil and the cunning of a deceitful spirit. There is also something else I know that happens contrary to what is fitting, on account of a man's choice that is not good. He lives isolated on every side, having neither brother nor son, yet thriving in many possessions; he lives in insatiability, and he is unwilling to give himself over to any goodness at all. One would gladly ask him: for whose sake does such a man toil, fleeing the doing of anything good headlong, while he is torn apart by manifold desires to acquire wealth?

problems.quote: thrown down by the violence of their oppressors, with no comfort at all anywhere
problems.source_quote: βίᾳ καταβεβλημένοι τῶν ἐπαμυνόντων, ἢ ὅλως παραμυθησομένων αὐτοὺς
problems.why: ἐπαμυνόντων means defenders. The victims lack defenders or comforters, and the English invents 'oppressors' and drops the missing defenders.
problems.fix: thrown down by force, with no one to defend them or comfort them at all, helplessness pressing on every side

problems.why: προστερνισάμενος means 'clasped to the breast', i.e. embraced the envy. 'Strikes his breast beforehand' is a wrong sense.
problems.fix: who takes it in and, as it were, clasps it to his breast

problems.quote: while he sets his heart on another's prosperity
problems.why: The envious man makes others' prosperity the cause of his grief. The English reads as if he desires that prosperity.
problems.fix: making the prosperity of others the cause of his grief

problems.quote: From all these reflections I turned back to myself and examined my thoughts
problems.source_quote: Ἀπὸ δὲ τούτων ἁπασῶν ἐμαυτὸν ἐπιστρέψας τῶν ἐννοιῶν κατεσκεψάμην
problems.why: He turns himself away from these thoughts and then examines; the thoughts are not what he inspects.
problems.fix: Turning myself away from all these reflections, I looked closely
problems.ruling: Ἀπὸ … τῶν ἐννοιῶν ἐμαυτὸν ἐπιστρέψας means turning away from these thoughts. The English reverses this into turning back to himself and examining his thoughts.

problems.quote: he is not willing to grant himself any kindness at all
problems.source_quote: χρηστότητι ἑαυτὸν οὐθ᾽ ὅλως ὁτιοῦν ἐπιδοῦναι θέλει
problems.why: The dative means he will not give himself to goodness at all, not that he withholds kindness from himself.
problems.fix: he is unwilling to give himself over to any goodness at all
problems.ruling: χρηστότητι ἑαυτὸν ἐπιδοῦναι means to devote or give himself to goodness. 'Grant himself kindness' wrongly makes him withhold kindness from himself.

fixed: Fixed 'thrown down by the violence of their oppressors, with no comfort at all anywhere' — ἐπαμυνόντων means defenders, not oppressors; the victims lack defenders/comforters and helplessness presses on every side (source: βίᾳ καταβεβλημένοι τῶν ἐπαμυνόντων, ἢ ὅλως παραμυθησομένων αὐτοὺς).
Fixed 'who strikes his breast beforehand' — προστερνισάμενος means 'clasped to the breast' (embraced the envy), not striking the breast beforehand (source: οἱονεὶ προστερνισάμενος).

Fixed 'while he sets his heart on another's prosperity' — τὴν τῶν ἄλλων εὐπραγίαν τιθέμενον means making others' prosperity the cause of his grief, not desiring it (source: τὴν τῶν ἄλλων εὐπραγίαν τιθέμενον).

Fixed 'From all these reflections I turned back to myself and examined my thoughts' — he turns away from the reflections then examines; the thoughts are not the object of inspection (source: Ἀπὸ δὲ τούτων ἁπασῶν ἐμαυτὸν ἐπιστρέψας τῶν ἐννοιῶν κατεσκεψάμην).

Fixed 'he is not willing to grant himself any kindness at all' — χρηστότητι ἑαυτὸν ... ἐπιδοῦναι θέλει means he will not give himself over to goodness, not that he withholds kindness from himself (source: χρηστότητι ἑαυτὸν οὐθ᾽ ὅλως ὁτιοῦν ἐπιδοῦναι θέλει).

last_rejected.why: First person “I would ask” becomes impersonal “one,” so the speaker no longer puts the question.
last_rejected.fix: I would gladly ask him: for whose sake does such a man toil
last_rejected.ruling: Optative ἐροίμην with ἂν is a potential 'I would ask'; 'One would gladly ask him' is generic phrasing, though first-person shift is minor; meaning of question unchanged.
